segments.text: American Fork City Council — Truth in Taxation Public Hearing — August 11, 2026:

stated he does not live in American Fork. Earlier this year, he was stopped in Farmington by an American Fork police officer under the false guise of an HOV violation. He stated the encounter escalated unnecessarily, with Officer Kitchen resorting to threats when he declined to comply with Officer Kitchen’s unlawful order. Officer Kitchen then refused to complete the purpose of the stop despite his requests for a citation so he could handle this in court. He noted he filed a complaint with the American Fork Police Department days later. Shortly after the recording of the stop went viral, Officer Kitchen then called and delivered a forced apology. Mr. Booker accepted that until he obtained a copy of the police report which was written after the apology and contained false statements. Mr. Booker stated that Officer Kitchen works as a school resource officer, and he felt the city should not allow this officer to continue serving as an SRO. The city’s inactions speak volumes and signal their willingness to tolerate abuse of authority. He noted that he will help motivate the city with a civil right lawsuit.

stated he was an accountant, so he loves numbers. To raise $502,000 in taxes, it increases the resident property tax by $33.41 per resident. He also knows that lawsuits are expensive, which includes legal and settlement fees. There are many future lawsuits that will come. That would be about $50 per resident. Why do the residents have to pay for the lawsuits? The residents are the ones who pay because of the city’s incapability to uphold the constitution. It comes out of their pockets.

has shared with them that he has been a victim of the police department twice, and he explained those incidents. He noted that for those incidents, he has received apology letters. He noted he shared with them two months ago and only Council Member Hunter reached out to him to make sure he was satisfied. In June, Council Member Hunter noted the threats they have received. He wanted to make it clear that there was no room for threats on anyone. He came here two weeks ago on his concerns of Officer Kitchen. It was okay to agree to disagree. He was glad he was on the side of protecting children. He hoped the city was right, but if he was right then they all lose.

stated she was one more voice that was concerned about the police force. She also had a weird incident several years ago. With her situation, and other situations, there seems to be lack of education or knowledge. She wanted to see more improvements for training. They needed to put victims first. She did not think it was being emphasized properly, and it was concerning.

stated he is a resident who has been here for many years. He was concerned about stewardship of finances. He mentioned the city had recently signed an agreement with CentraCom. He has heard about lawsuits, and he has asked for a citizens review board. They also put up a big curb extension by his house that will be a hazard for bikes. He appreciated what they did, but he was concerned about some of the expenses.

thanked them for the opportunity to speak. She was a resident of the county but frequents American Fork. They still have not seen accountability and transparency within the Police Department. While she supports police departments, she was disappointed and does not trust this department or city. She wondered what it would take to get an interview with the mayor about what was going on.

stated he lives in the more historic part of the city. He understands the need for property taxes to maintain infrastructure. However, he was reminded of the wisdom of Benjamin Franklin who said to be cautious of the small expenses; a small leak will sink a mighty ship. A previous citizen noted that they should make small incremental tax increases, but he did not agree with that. Mr. Grahm stated there may have been a great amount of deliberation, but he feels like there is not much proof of the deliberation or of their due diligence. He requested a more robust explanation on the cuts in the budget. If they are making those cuts, they could increase those cuts slightly more to reach a more equitable tax increase. He also asked for greater clarity on the fire fighter’s wages. He was also concerned about the police and flock cameras. He also requested the council bring back the original comments section to provide feedback on the city’s website; the system was changed and he was not sure where to find it.

stated for years he was the pressman that printed the AF Citizen from 1980 to 2005. He was a concerned citizen wondering what was going on with the police department. He asked if there would be a meeting where the citizens would be told what was going on. He asked if they would be held accountable.

entities.speaker: Bradley J. Frost
entities.remark-context: Response to request for an AFPD accountability meeting

segments.text: After Julie Rodriguez said she had not seen accountability or transparency within AFPD, did not trust the department or city, and wanted an interview with the mayor, Mayor Bradley Frost asked her to provide her information to the city recorder. The published minutes do not record a substantive response to her concerns.

entities.label: Mayor’s follow-up to an AFPD accountability concern

segments.text: Julie Rodriguez asked how she could obtain an interview with the mayor about AFPD accountability and transparency. Mayor Bradley Frost requested her contact information, but the published minutes do not record a substantive response to the concerns she raised.
Relevant passage from the official meeting minutes:

Julie Rodriguez stated that residents still had not seen accountability and transparency within the Police Department. While she supported police departments, she said she was disappointed and did not trust the department or city. She asked what it would take to get an interview with the mayor about what was going on.

Mayor Frost asked her to provide her information to the city recorder.
